newsitem.title: USA: Motorola makes sector management changes.
newsitem.headline: Motorola makes sector management changes.

text.p: Technology giant Motorola Inc said Monday it made various changes in the top management of two of its largest business sectors.

James Norling was named president and general manager of the Messaging, Information and Media Sector, effective January 1. He replaces Robert Growney, who was recently appointed president and chief operating officer of Motorola Inc.
Norling previously served as executive vice president of Motorola Inc, and president of Motorola Europe, Middle East and Africa, the company said.

Hector Ruiz will become executive vice president in the office of the president, Semiconductor Products Sector, effective February 15, 1997. He will work with Thomas George, president and general manager of the sector, who plans to retire later in the year. Ruiz will become sector president on May 15, Motorola said.
Ruiz currently serves as executive vice president and general manager of the Messaging Systems Products Group.

"These changes, along with those announced earlier in our cellular, space and computer businesses, set the stage for renewed profitable growth across a large portion of our product portfolio," said Christopher Galvin, who will become chief executive officer on January 1.
On December 9, Motorola said Edward Staiano will retire as president of its General Systems Sector to become vice chairman and chief executive officer of Iridium LLC, effective January 1.
The company also named Jack Scanlon president and general manager of the new Cellular Networks and Space Sector, and Robert Weisshappel general manager of its Cellular Subscriber Group.
